title: Home page narrates its own thirty-second pitch
description:
Put the product on the home page doing its own elevator pitch, so a
visitor can hear what Auritus does instead of only reading about it.

## Behaviour

A "Hear it for yourself" section sits directly after the hero. The panel is
shaped like a publisher article with the embed above it — which is what a
page carrying Auritus actually looks like. The copy in the panel is both
what you read and what the player speaks: 76 spoken words, about thirty
seconds at a normal narration pace, opening with "Press play. What you
hear is this page reading itself." The credit line carries
`data-auritus-ignore` so it is not read aloud.

The player's CSS variables point at the site tokens rather than a second
set of colours, so the embed follows the newsprint palette in both schemes
with nothing to keep in sync.

## Hero copy

Cut the headline to make room for it. "Let every article speak. Keep the
choices that matter." was two headlines: the second sentence restates the
section below it, which already carries that framing as "Control is the
product", and at five wrapped lines the type could not do its job. Cut to
the first sentence and raised the size. The hero intro had the same
duplication — its last sentence repeated the three choice cards verbatim —
so it is one sentence now.

## Proven

Content hash `2caf28aa` returns `done` with a signed `audio_url`; the
player reports "Ready" and renders a single card. Verified in a real
browser, not the in-app preview pane, which blocks the cross-origin job
call and is not a valid environment for this.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: The home page demonstrates narration on itself
  Scenario: A visitor hears what Auritus does
    Given the home page carries the Auritus embed over its demo article
    When the visitor presses play
    Then the page narrates its own description
    And the narration runs about thirty seconds
    And the credit line is not read aloud
```
